jobDescription:
ML Platform Engineer — Model Infrastructure

We're hiring an ML Platform Engineer to build the infrastructure that trains, serves, and monitors machine-learning models at scale. You'll own the tooling and pipelines that let research teams ship models reliably.

Requirements:
- Strong Python for platform and tooling work
- PyTorch for model training and evaluation workflows
- Docker for containerizing training and serving workloads
- Kubernetes for orchestrating those workloads in production
- Apache Spark for large-scale distributed feature computation
- Apache Kafka for streaming features and events between services
- PostgreSQL for platform metadata and run tracking
- Terraform for provisioning infrastructure as code
- MLflow for experiment tracking and a model registry
- CI/CD for automated build, test, and deployment
- AWS as the primary production cloud
resume:
Alex Moreno
ML Platform Engineer

Summary
ML platform engineer with 7 years building the training and serving infrastructure behind production machine-learning systems. I focus on the tooling and pipelines that let research teams ship models reliably, from experiment to endpoint.

Experience

Staff ML Platform Engineer — Northwind AI (2021–present)
- Owned the internal ML platform end to end; Python was the primary language across every service, SDK, and CLI I built.
- Built training utilities and evaluation harnesses on top of PyTorch, standardizing how research teams fine-tuned and benchmarked models.
- Packaged every model and service into containers before rollout, with a reproducible base image pinned per framework version.
- Operated model-serving workloads on K8s, including autoscaling, rolling upgrades, and GPU scheduling across node pools.
- Ran large-scale feature computation as distributed batch jobs across a shared compute cluster, processing billions of rows nightly.
- Streamed feature updates and inference events through a durable, partitioned event log with exactly-once delivery guarantees.
- Stored feature metadata, lineage, and run records in Postgres, with every schema migration gated in review.
- Provisioned clusters and cloud resources through version-controlled infrastructure-as-code, peer-reviewed on every change.
- Automated build, test, and deployment for every platform component with GitHub Actions.

ML Engineer — Cartwright Labs (2017–2021)
- Trained and shipped classification and ranking models in Python and PyTorch.
- Built our own lightweight experiment tracker and model registry in-house rather than adopting MLflow, which the team evaluated but chose not to run.

Notes
- Our infrastructure ran entirely on-prem and on GCP. I have not worked hands-on with AWS.
